title: compact-failure-atlas-zara
content:
Purpose: quick lightweight artifact to capture recurring small failure modes across short A/B runs — not a formal report, more of a scratch atlas to help triage regexable problems and decide what to add to the canonical test set.

Context: ran a ~2k sample sweep across customer-chat workload (seq len median ~120) during the 2024-09 minimal latency experiment (canary group). Models compared: redwood-v1-7b (float), redwood-v1-7b-8bit (quant), redwood-v1-13b (float, slower baseline). Focus: hallucination of numeric facts, instruction-follow failures, truncated streaming outputs.

Quick rubric (ad-hoc, for this spike):
- 0 = correct/acceptable (no action)
- 1 = minor formatting or clarity issue (add to micro-heuristics)
- 2 = incorrect or missing required info (add unit test & sample prompt)
- 3 = safety/contradiction or systemic hallucination (investigate model/rollout)

Observations (grouped by failure archetype):
1) Number hallucination (freq ~1.6% in quant runs, ~0.9% in float)
- example prompt: "Summarize last quarter revenue in 2 bullets with % change vs prior quarter."
- v1-7b output: "Revenue: $3.2M, up 18% vs prior quarter." (ground truth: $2.9M, up 10%) -> score 2 (tends to hallucinate one-off digits)
- v1-7b-8bit output: "Revenue: $4.1M, up 41% vs prior quarter." -> score 3 (systemic inflation pattern in quantized run)
- notes: common when prompt asks for arithmetic comparison; sometimes returns plausible but incorrect percentages. Add to eval set: 12 arithmetic/compare prompts. Consider: disable numeric-consolidation heuristic for quant until we add a calibration pass.

2) Instruction drop on multi-step tasks (freq ~2.7% overall)
- example prompt: "Give me a 3-step checklist for onboarding a new API key with permissions and rotation schedule."
- v1-13b: returns only 2 steps (missing rotation schedule) -> score 2
- v1-7b-8bit: returns 4 steps but merges rotation schedule into step 3 awkwardly -> score 1
- notes: sometimes streaming chunk boundaries coincide with last-step truncation; add streaming cut heuristics in console (small test: increase chunk buffer by 20 tokens for these workflows).

3) Overly apologetic / hedging on factual answers (UX regression)
- Prompts: single-fact queries where older baseline gave direct answer, current model prepends hedging "I may be mistaken" in ~6% of hits -> score 1
- Impact: user-facing tone degraded; product wants directness for this type of query. Action: add tone-checker rule (if prompt tagged as factual-short, require <=2 hedging tokens).

Micro-actions taken during spike:
- Collected 200 failure exemplars into /tmp/eval-spike-2024-09 (pushed to eval bucket: s3://redwood-evals/spike-2024-09/compact-failure-atlas.json)
- Opened JIRA-7892 to track numeric hallucination triage (linked above)
- Quick patch deployed to canary: prefix-template tweak to require explicit ask-for-sources (temporary) — reduced % of 3-score numeric hallucinations from 1.6%->0.9% in next 500 samples.

Hypotheses to test (next 48–72h):
- H1: Quantization induces scalar rounding that is amplified when model synthesizes arithmetic -> reproduce with synthetic arithmetic-only sweep.
- H2: Streaming chunk boundaries correlate with dropped final steps -> reproduce by instrumenting token timestamps.
- H3: Prompt templates that include explicit "provide numbers only" reduce numeric hallucination but may worsen terse hedging -> run A/B with tone constraint.

Proposed short-term checklist (for prod folks / SRE / canary owners):
- Add 12 arithmetic prompts to smoke tests (conservative sample).
- Add a rule in Console to tag routes as "factual-short" and apply tone limiter.
- Add telemetry flag to log token-chunk indices for streaming responses (low overhead).
- Schedule 1h triage with model-onboarding team (include quant specialist) next week.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep this doc compact; move canonical examples to confluence once validated.
- Consider adding a tiny eval harness that runs inside the canary pod (local smoke tests) to catch the numeric inflation before external rollout.
- Follow up with Priya on whether we can re-run quant repro on different hardware (A100 vs H100) — currently only tested on A100-40GB.

Raw sample captures (copied verbatim):
- P: "What was the total number of new signups last month?"
  R(v1-7b): "About 12,400 new signups."  // GT: 11,328 -> score 2
  R(v1-7b-8bit): "Nearly 15k signups." // score 3

- P: "3-step checklist to rotate API keys for service X"
  R(v1-13b): "1) Revoke old key 2) Create new key" // missing rotation schedule -> score 2
  R(v1-7b-8bit): "1) Create new key 2) Update services 3) Revoke old key 4) Document schedule" // awkward merge -> score 1

Questions/open:
- Is the numeric inflation correlated with prompt length? initial look: slightly higher on longer prompts (>200 tokens). Need controlled sweep.
- Does reducing temperature help? quick test shows marginal improvement but hurts diversity. Not ideal.

Next edits: convert top 10 exemplars to confluence page and tag related unit tests. If anyone wants more raw samples I pushed the full capture to the eval bucket.

-- zara
